collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — BELIEF, IDENTITY AND PERSONAL EXPRESSION (BLF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Religious, spiritual, atheist, agnostic, questioning and simply uninterested villagers living side by side; who people are, whom they love and how they present themselves. Privacy is respected, nobody has to explain or justify anything, and differences don't have to be the subject. Gods and spirits stay unconfirmed either way.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager sits alone on the hill at every full moon, and a friend worries about the dark: offer to go too, or let them go.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: On nights when the moon is full, (subject) walks alone to the top of the hill and sits there until it sets. It's how (subject.he/she) feels close to whatever (subject.he/she) believes in. (friend), (subject.his/her) friend, worries about (subject.him/her) walking alone in the dark, and tonight says so.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I'll come with you," says (friend). (subject) hesitates. "It's a quiet thing. I sit and don't talk." "I can do that," says (friend). They go up the hill together. (friend) is very bad at not talking for the first hour. Then (friend.he/she) gets the hang of it. They watch the moon set. "Same time next month?" asks (friend). (subject) thinks. "Maybe every other month."

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Be careful," says (friend), and lets (subject.him/her) go. (subject) climbs the hill, sits, and watches the moon. It's quiet and enormous up there. (subject.He/she) comes back at dawn and finds (friend) dozing outside (subject.his/her) hut with a torch. "You waited?" "I couldn't sleep," says (friend). "I didn't come up, though." (subject) is grateful for both things.
